name: Example: Finding a Quartic Polynomial Given Two Real and Two Complex Roots
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14066605/assets/658fa5a494ef01b5924847335ce863aa8c6b5f8adee5ee97967a8c8bebd83a80.png)

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$
worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x_1=-2},$ ${x_2=3},$ and ${x_{3,4}=1 \pm 3\textrm{i}}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is ${a=1}.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1\cdot (x-(-2))(x-(3))(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i})) \\  & =(x+2)(x-3)(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)(x-3)(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i})) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-3x+2x-6)({x}^{2}-x(1-3\text{i})-x(1+3\text{i})+(1+3\text{i})(1-3\text{i})) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-x-6)({x}^{2}-2x+10) & = \\ {x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+10{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-10x-6{x}^{2}+12x-60 & = \\ {x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+2x-60 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x) = x^4 - 3x^3 + 6x^2 + 2x - 60.$
